replacements.old: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said Tuesday that he would support a quarter point rate increase in December. CNBC reports that he spoke in London and said a half point move should be considered if inflation runs hotter than expected.
replacements.new: Before Tuesday’s inflation release, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said that he would support a quarter point rate increase in December. CNBC reports that he spoke in London and said a half point move should be considered if inflation runs hotter than expected.

replacements.old: His remarks came hours before the October consumer price index release. Bloomberg reports that economists expect prices to rise 0.3% for the month, after a 0.6% increase previously. Yahoo Finance reports that stock futures were little changed after Monday’s rally.
replacements.new: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, after a 0.6% increase in September. Core prices, excluding food and energy, rose 0.3%, matching September. Both monthly figures are seasonally adjusted. BLS did not publish annual headline or core rates because the October 2025 indexes were unavailable following last year’s lapse in appropriations.

replacements.old: Why it matters. Higher rates raise borrowing costs for households and businesses. Bloomberg reports that two year yields rose as traders moved to fully price in a December increase. The Fed’s next policy meeting is scheduled for Dec. 8 and 9, according to CNBC.
